title: One line of numerals under the colophon of a sira manuscript dated 732 AH (BnF Arabe 1966; catalogue 2890)

documents.shelfmark: Paris, BnF, Département des Manuscrits, Arabe 1966, last written page (Gallica btv1b11001551n, view 50)
documents.date: after Jumada I 732 AH (Feb 1332); the line is undated

plaintext.source: None. The black words at the right of the line are the end of the colophon's blessing, not a gloss; the two notes below are collation notes.

transcription.source: BnF IIIF crop of view 50 at native resolution (2,329 x 533 px), enlarged four times
transcription.notes: Black-and-white microfilm. The 4 (twice) could be a 3 and the 9 (three times) a 6. The catalogue entry counted about 28 numerals and took the colophon's last words for part of the cipher; 23 numerals are there.

system.summary: Twenty-three Eastern Arabic numerals in one line without zeros, dots or visible division, seven distinct digits; the system is not identified.
system.notes: No 0, 3 or 6. Read right to left, '1 2' occurs four times. The line cuts cleanly into 16 or 17 numbers no larger than 28. It may not be a text at all.

prior_solution.where: None found: de Slane no. 1966 only notes the line; DECODE, Cryptiana and web searches (catalogue vetting, 15 Nov 2026) and Gacek's Vademecum found no reading.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: the user posed the target by its catalogue number; no target-specific intervention.
tools: Sahih al-Bukhari text (hadith-json) as a classical vocabulary
Internet Archive full text of Gacek's Vademecum

solution.what: Fetched view 50 through the BnF IIIF route (line crop at native resolution, lower half of the page at 1,800 px).
Transcribed the line from fourfold enlargements: 23 numerals. The dark words at its right end are the colophon's 'ila yawm al-din', not cipher.
Counts and adjacency: 7 distinct digits, no 0, 3 or 6; '1 2' four times right to left; clean cuts into 16 or 17 numbers up to 28; glyph spacing measured, no groups.
Letters by abjad value with zeros lost (reduced abjad), both directions, word segmentation (abjad_seg.py); repeated with 4 as 3 and 9 as 6.
Whole-word abjad sums run together (wordsum.py, wordsum2.py): every cut finds words, so the test decides nothing.
Alphabet positions 1 to 28 in four orders, from either end, all cuts, both directions (ordinal.py); shifts and affine maps mod 28 on the two clean cuts (shift.py).

One digit one letter: depth-first word segmentation with 1 and 2 fixed to alif and lam (subst.py, classical.py), then to every ordered pair of letters in both directions with a vocabulary from Sahih al-Bukhari (allpairs.py). Best strings are word salad.
Place-marker digits, strokes as zeros or separators, digit pairs (table, abjad words, aiq-bakr groups), and non-text readings (horoscope, sira numbers, buduh square, doubling series), worked by hand.
Looked at all 54 views as contact sheets for more writing in the pale numeral hand; read the two notes under the line (collation notes, one dated Rajab 734).

Gacek, Arabic Manuscripts: A Vademecum for Readers (Internet Archive full text): entries on secret alphabets, abjad, popular culture; two web searches on numeral cryptograms in colophons. No description of such a cipher, no mention of this manuscript.

Digit as digital root of the letter's place in four alphabet orders (classes.py), and digit pairs as addends of a letter value; searched for the edition of Ibn al-Durayhim's Miftah al-kunuz (not online in full).
Second session: independent re-reading of the native-resolution crop and a light-end contrast stretch. Result: the same 23 numerals; the second from the right may be a 3.
Isomorph search of three tokenisations in both directions against the Qur'an and nine hadith collections (iso_quran.py, iso_hadith.py).

Reduced abjad values and digital roots after each of 28 alphabet shifts (reduced_shift.py); digit plus zero-count marker, every parse (marker.py); whole-word abjad sums with a colophon lexicon (ws.py); letter positions in the basmala.

Independent agent: own transcription (same 23 numerals); shuffle test of the repeats; eight further families (multiplied values, non-modular affine, key-text index, difference and running-key forms, letter-name values, other alphabets, stroke dividers, non-text number series).

outcome.method_basis: Eleven families of numeral system were tested on the 23 digits and none gives a reading; the line is too short, with no word division, key or second text in the same hand.

gaps.detail: Seven symbols over 23 places with no word division, no second text in the same hand and no key; every standard numeral system tested fails. The colour scan would settle the doubtful shapes and whether dots were lost.

outcome.notes: Left in progress, 15 Nov 2026. Catalogue 2890 stays in the catalogue.
